description: Recommend what to watch on a flight from the airline's in-flight catalogue, ranked by IMDb rating and the user's taste. Use when the user asks what to watch on their flight or plane, what movies are on Emirates / ice, United, KLM, British Airways, Singapore Airlines, Lufthansa, JAL, Cathay Pacific, Qantas, ANA or American Airlines this month, for plane movie picks, or whether a specific film is available on a given airline. # Inflight movie picker

Local monthly catalogues for Emirates, United, KLM, British Airways (`ba`), Singapore Airlines (`singapore`),
Lufthansa, Japan Airlines (`jal`), Cathay Pacific (`cathay`), Qantas, ANA and American (`american`),
matched to IMDb and ranked by a blend of IMDb, Letterboxd, RT and Metacritic plus the user's Letterboxd taste and `taste.json`. Run everything from the project root `/home/lensky/Dev/plane_movie`
with bun (`~/.bun/bin` on PATH). `bun run cli` with no arguments lists the registered airline ids.

## Answering "what should I watch on my flight?"

1. Find out the airline and, if it matters, the flight month (catalogues change monthly).
2. Make sure data is fresh, then rank:
   ```bash
   bun run cli stats --airline united                  # snapshot for this month? match rate?
   bun run cli fetch united [--month YYYY-MM]          # only if the month is missing (cached per month)
   bun run cli match --airline united                  # after any fetch or imdb sync
   bun run cli picks --airline united --top 15 [--genre Thriller] [--min-rating 7] [--language English] [--min-year N] [--max-year N] [--year N]
   ```
   `picks` defaults to Emirates when `--airline` is omitted.
3. Present 5-10 picks with one line each: why it fits (genre, rating), runtime (fits the flight?), IMDb link.
4. For "is X on the plane?": `bun run cli search "<title>"` searches every fetched airline (or `--airline X`).

`bun run cli imdb sync` reloads IMDb (downloads ~1.2 GB if files are older than 7 days, ~3 min load). Only run it
when `stats` shows 0 IMDb titles or the user asks for fresher ratings.

## Taste and ratings

The simplest taste input is the user's IMDb export: imdb.com > Your Ratings (and Watchlist) > three-dot menu > Export, CSVs dropped into `data/imdb-ratings/`, then `bun run cli taste import` (joined on tconst, no title matching).
A Letterboxd export works too. If `picks` prints "taste: taste.json only", offer this:

1. Letterboxd > Settings > Data > Export your data; drop the zip into `data/letterboxd/`.
2. `bun run cli taste import` (re-run after each new export; it replaces the previous import and lists unmatched
   films). Watched and rated films are then excluded, watchlist films are boosted, and genre/director affinities
   learned from the ratings show up as "you rate X +0.7 (3 films)" reasons.

Extra rating sources (optional, slow the first time): `bun run cli ids sync`, then
`bun run cli ratings sync [--source letterboxd|rt|mc|tmdb] [--airline X]`. Scraped sites go at 1 request/s with a
30-day cache, so a first full run is about an hour per source; scope it with `--airline` or `--limit N`. TMDB needs
`TMDB_API_KEY` in `.env` (free key from themoviedb.org > Settings > API) and is skipped otherwise. Picks then blend
IMDb, Letterboxd, RT audience and Metacritic; each pick shows its LB, RT and MC scores on its first line.

`taste.json` stays as manual overrides: `liked_genres`, `disliked_genres` (IMDb names such as Sci-Fi, Thriller,
Horror), `min_rating`, `min_votes`, `seen` (titles or tt ids, excluded from picks), `favourites` (titles; their
directors get a small boost). When the user says they have seen a film, add it to `seen`.

## Caveats to tell the user when relevant

- All sources are undocumented airline endpoints: personal, low-volume use. Never fetch the same airline-month more
  than once a day (raw responses are cached under `data/raw/`; `--refresh` forces a refetch). Never loop retries,
  especially against BA (Akamai).
- BA, Singapore and Qantas only publish the current cycle, so next month cannot be fetched for them until it starts.
  The others accept a future `--month`. Lufthansa, JAL and ANA make one detail call per film (~130-410 requests,
  cached), so do not refetch them casually.
- Qantas is the large international seatback catalogue; domestic and smaller aircraft differ.
- Matches are graded high/medium/low/none from title, year, director and runtime. Picks use only high and medium.
  Emirates has no year field, so its regional-language films and concert specials match least often.
- A catalogue can differ by route, aircraft or country; only the airline's public web catalogue is fetched.

# Inflight movie picker (Claude app)

Seatback Cinema holds every film in eleven airlines' seatback catalogues for the current month, with IMDb ids,
ratings and a short synopsis. You reach it one of two ways, and they answer the same: the `seatback` connector's
tools when they're available (`list_airlines`, `catalogue`, `picks`, `profile_from_imdb_url`,
`profile_from_letterboxd`, `profile_from_text`, `save_profile`, `get_profile`), otherwise the GET API at
`https://seatback.len5ky.com/api/` through your web fetch tool (the last section maps each tool to a URL). Check
for the tools first; most people have only the skill, so the API is the usual route. You recommend from what comes
back and from nothing else. If a film isn't in a result, it isn't on the plane as far as you know, however well it
would fit. Never fall back to recommending from memory.

## 1. The flight

You need the airline, the flight length and whether children are watching. Take what the person already said and
ask for the rest in one short message. If they just want picks, assume (long-haul, adults) and say what you
assumed.

Call `list_airlines` once to get the airline ids and the month each catalogue covers. Covered: Emirates, United,
KLM, British Airways, Singapore, Lufthansa, JAL, Cathay Pacific, Qantas, ANA, American. Delta, Turkish, Air France
and Qatar aren't covered because they don't publish a usable catalogue. Say that plainly; don't guess their
line-up. If the flight is next month and the airline hasn't published it yet, use the current month and say the
line-up may change around the 1st.

Flight length becomes `flight_minutes` (7 hours is 420). `picks` drops anything longer than the flight minus 30
minutes, which covers taxi, climb and descent. Children watching means `filters: { family: true }`, and you still
check each pick's `cert` against the child's age yourself.

## 2. Their taste

People see this part, so a word on naming: the saved profile is their **taste code**. Never call it a token in
anything you write to them, even though the tool field is `token`.

Use the first of these the person can give you, in this order: an IMDb profile link, a Letterboxd username, a
taste code from last time. If they already sent one, use it and don't ask. Otherwise, when taste matters (they want
picks, not a yes or no on one title), ask in one line, in your own words:

> Want these ranked for you? Paste your IMDb profile link or your Letterboxd username, or your taste code if you
> have one from last time.

If they have none of those, or would rather not share, go to the seen check below. Bring up exports and file
uploads only if they ask, or if everything else has failed.

### A taste code

It's 20 lowercase letters and digits, usually pasted as "My Seatback Cinema taste code is abcd...". Older ones say
"profile token" instead; treat them the same. Pass `profile: { token: "..." }` straight to `picks` and skip the
other routes, even if they also pasted a profile link. Call `get_profile` only when you need to show them what's in
it. If the code comes back unknown or expired, say so in plain words and ask for the link or the username.

### An IMDb profile link

It looks like `https://www.imdb.com/user/p.xxxxxxxx/ratings/` (older ones use `ur1234567` in place of `p.xxx`), and
the ratings must be public. Call `profile_from_imdb_url` with the link straight away. Don't fetch the IMDb pages
yourself first: the connector reads the profile on its own server, scores and watchlist included, in up to half a
minute for a big one. It answers with counts, the genres and directors it learned, `notes` and an `imdb_user` id.
Pass `profile: { imdb_user: "ur..." }` to `picks` and mention anything in `notes`. Call it once per link: the
import stays on the server for 24 hours, so later picks in the same chat reuse `imdb_user`.

When it fails, the error says why. Don't call it again with the same link.

- **Private ratings.** Tell them how to fix it in one line: on imdb.com, Settings, then Privacy, and set ratings to
  public; then send the link again. Meanwhile offer Letterboxd or the seen check.
- **IMDb said no, or the daily limit is reached.** Say the IMDb import isn't working right now, in a few words,
  and move on to their Letterboxd username or the seen check.

### A Letterboxd username

Any `https://letterboxd.com/<username>/` link will do as well. Call `profile_from_letterboxd` with it and pass the
`profile` it returns to `picks` unchanged. It reads their public diary, which only goes back 50 entries, so tell
them in your reply that you went by their latest 50 logged films. Older films they've seen can still turn up, so
follow with one round of the seen check on the picks.

### The seen check

Most of what a long rating history buys is knowing what they've already watched. Without one, ask:

1. Call `picks` with whatever profile you have (none is fine) and `limit: 20`.
2. Show the top ten as one short list, title and year only, and ask which they've seen. A reply like "seen 2, 5
   and Wicked" is enough.
3. Add the ones they name to the profile's `seen` as their `imdbId`s, call `picks` again, and ask once more about
   the next ten they haven't been shown.
4. Then pick from the third call. Two rounds at most, even if they've seen a lot.

If they mention films they loved or hated along the way, add those to `seen` too, and put any genres they want or
want to avoid in `liked_genres` and `disliked_genres`. Keep each round to two lines.

### Files, if they ask

An IMDb ratings export (CSV), a Letterboxd export (zip) or its CSVs, attached to the chat, still work. Send each
file's text to `profile_from_text`, unchanged, and chain the files with `add_to`:

- IMDb ratings export (`Const` and `Your Rating` columns): `kind: "imdb_csv"`. A watchlist or list export (`Const`
  without `Your Rating`, or one that starts with `Position`) is detected; add `list: "watchlist"` to be sure.
- Letterboxd `ratings.csv` and `watched.csv`: `kind: "letterboxd_csv"`. `watchlist.csv`: the same with
  `list: "watchlist"`.

Unpack a Letterboxd zip with your file tool or code sandbox and send those three files; skip `profile.csv`, which
holds their email and no films. A file over about 200 KB goes in parts of about 200 KB cut at line ends, each part
starting with the file's header line, each call after the first passing the previous result as `add_to`.

The IMDb export is at https://www.imdb.com/list/ratings/export on a computer (it appears under Your exports a
minute later); Letterboxd's is under Settings, Data, Export your data. For a big export, or a phone where attaching
a file is awkward, https://seatback.len5ky.com/taste turns the same files into a taste code in their browser.

## 3. Offer a taste code (once)

After the first import that worked (an IMDb link or a file), offer it once, in one line: "Want a taste code so
next time you can skip this? It holds your film ids and scores, nothing else, for a year." If they say yes, call
`save_profile` with `profile: { imdb_user: "ur..." }` after an IMDb import, or with the profile itself after a file,
and give them the code on its own line with the sentence to paste next time: "My Seatback Cinema taste code is
<code>." Anyone with the code can load

# Inflight movie picker

Seatback Cinema publishes every film in eleven airlines' seatback catalogues, month by month, and matches about
94% of them to an IMDb id. `scripts/catalogue.ts` in this skill's folder downloads one airline-month, caches it
and prints it as a table. You pick from that table and nothing else: if a film isn't in it, it isn't on the plane
as far as you know.

Use it when someone asks what to watch on a flight, whether a film is on an airline, or what an airline is showing
this month. Don't use it for streaming or cinema recommendations.

## 1. Get the facts about the flight

You need four things. Take whatever the person already said and ask for the rest in one short message; if they
just want picks, guess sensibly and say what you assumed.

- **Airline**, and the month if the flight is in a later month than today (catalogues change around the 1st).
- **Flight length.** Long-haul is 6 hours or more, short-haul under 3.
- **Who is watching.** Alone, with a partner, or with children (ages matter).
- **Mood.** Something easy, something to cry at, a film they've been meaning to see.

Airline ids: `emirates`, `united`, `klm`, `ba`, `singapore`, `lufthansa`, `jal`, `cathay`, `qantas`, `ana`,
`american`. Delta, Turkish, Air France and Qatar aren't covered (they don't publish a full catalogue, or hide it
behind bot protection). Say so plainly and offer general picks they can check against the seatback screen.

## 2. Read the catalogue

Run the script by its full path from the person's working directory, so relative paths to their exports work.
Any of Bun, Node 22.6+ or Deno will run it:

```bash
S=<this skill's folder>/scripts/catalogue.ts
bun $S --list                                     # airline ids and published months
bun $S emirates                                   # latest month
bun $S united 2026-11 --max-runtime 110           # a given month, films up to 110 minutes
bun $S united --family --max-runtime 100         # kids: family, kids and animation genres
bun $S ba --search "wicked"                       # "is X on the plane?"
node --experimental-strip-types $S klm            # Node; deno run -A $S klm for Deno
```

The table is `title | year | min | genres | cert | imdb`. `cert` is the airline's own age rating (PG13, 12, M,
TV-G and so on; formats vary by airline). `imdb` is the matched IMDb id; `(medium)` after it means the match rests
on one signal, such as runtime alone, so treat it as probably right. `-` means no confident match: the film is on
the plane, but you can't vouch for which film it is.

Other options: `--matched` (only films with an IMDb id), `--tmdb` (adds TMDB score and vote count; needs
`TMDB_API_KEY`), `--taste <path>`, `--imdb-url <url>` and `--letterboxd-url <url>` (below), `--profile-token <token>`,
`--save-profile`, `--json`, `--refresh`. Emirates lists about 2,000 films and Cathay
about 1,500, so filter by genre or runtime, or read the full list once and shortlist from it.

If the flight month isn't published yet, use the latest month and tell the person the line-up may change.

## 3. Learn their taste

Look in the working directory first, without asking: an IMDb export (`data/imdb-ratings/*.csv`, or any CSV with a
`Const` column) or an unzipped Letterboxd export (`ratings.csv`, `watched.csv`, `watchlist.csv`) beats anything
else. Pass the file or folder to the script with `--taste data/imdb-ratings` (or the export folder).

Otherwise ask for the first of these they can give, in this order: an IMDb profile link, a Letterboxd username, a
taste code from last time. With none of them, do the seen check below. Mention exports only if they ask or
everything else failed.

**IMDb link.** Pass it to the script. It reads the profile from this machine through IMDb's API (the calls
imdb.com makes in a browser; a 941-rating profile with scores and watchlist is 7 requests), falls back to the
profile pages, and caches it for 24 hours. The ratings must be public: if the script or the connector says they're
private, tell them in one line to set ratings to public under Settings, Privacy on imdb.com and send the link
again. IMDb refuses scripted requests from some networks (an empty HTTP 202 or a 429). Then, if the Seatback Cinema
connector is in this session (tools `list_airlines`, `picks`, `profile_from_imdb_url` and so on), call
`profile_from_imdb_url` with the link once; it reads the profile from its own server and usually gets through. Pass
`profile: { imdb_user }` from its answer to `picks`. Without the connector, the same server answers
`curl 'https://seatback.len5ky.com/api/profile?imdb=<link>'` with a taste code, and
`/api/picks?airline=<id>&flight_minutes=<n>&code=<taste code>` with ranked cards.

**Letterboxd username.** `--letterboxd-url https://letterboxd.com/<username>/` reads their films pages, 72 a page,
then the watchlist, up to 50 pages. If Letterboxd answers 403, the connector's `profile_from_letterboxd` reads their
diary feed instead, which covers only the latest 50 entries; say so, and follow with the seen check.

```bash
bun $S emirates --imdb-url https://www.imdb.com/user/ur12345678/ratings/
bun $S ba --letterboxd-url https://letterboxd.com/<username>/
bun $S emirates --profile-token <code>
```

**Taste code.** "My Seatback Cinema taste code is ..." (or the older "my profile token is ...") goes in as
`--profile-token <code>`, in place of the other options. To carry a profile into the Claude app, add
`--save-profile` to an `--imdb-url`, `--letterboxd-url` or `--taste` run: it stores the profile on the Seatback
server and ends with the sentence to paste there.

With any of these the script hides every film they've rated or logged, adds a `you` column that says `watchlist`
for films on their watchlist, and prints their 9-10/10 films and their 1-4/10 films above the table. IMDb rows
match on the IMDb id, exactly. Letterboxd rows have no IMDb id, so they match through the dataset's Letterboxd
links where it has them, else on title (lowercased, accents, punctuation and a leading "The" dropped) with the year
within one. Letterboxd half-stars are doubled to the 10-point scale.

**The seen check.** Most of what a long rating history buys is knowing what they've already watched. With nothing
else, shortlist the 20 strongest films for the flight from the table, show the first ten as title and year, and
ask which they've seen; then ask once more about the next ten. Two rounds at most. Drop every film they name, and
note any they say they loved or hated, plus anything to avoid (horror, subtitles, sad endings).

When everything else has failed, the export is the fallback: imdb.com, Your ratings, the three-dot menu, Export,
or Letterboxd's Settings, Data, Export your data; then `--taste`.

## 4. Rank

The dataset carries no review scores. Rank with what you know about each film: its reception, who it suits, how
close it sits to the films they loved and how far from the ones they hated. If `TMDB_API_KEY` is set, run with
`--tmdb` and use the score and vote count as a check on your memory; a 7.8 from 40 votes means little. Never
invent a score.

Watchlist films go near the top unless they clash with the flight (a three-hour epic on a 90-minute hop). Prefer
this year's and last year's releases when they're good: those are the films people can't easily watch at home.

evidence.quote: Seatback Cinema publishes every film in eleven airlines' seatback catalogues, month by month, and matches about 94% of them to an IMDb id.
Use it when someone asks what to watch on a flight, whether a film is on an airline, or what an airline is showing this month.
`scripts/catalogue.ts` in this skill's folder downloads one airline-month, caches it and prints it as a table.
The table is `title | year | min | genres | cert | imdb`.
bun $S united --family --max-runtime 100         # kids: family, kids and animation genres
bun $S ba --search "wicked"                       # "is X on the plane?"
If `TMDB_API_KEY` is set, run with `--tmdb` and use the score and vote count as a check on your memory
**Airline**, and the month if the flight is in a later month than today (catalogues change around the 1st).
an IMDb export (`data/imdb-ratings/*.csv`, or any CSV with a `Const` column) or an unzipped Letterboxd export (`ratings.csv`, `watched.csv`, `watchlist.csv`) beats anything else.
**Taste code.** "My Seatback Cinema taste code is ..." (or the older "my profile token is ...") goes in as `--profile-token <code>`
it stores the profile on the Seatback server and ends with the sentence to paste there.
